title: I watch TikToks so my agents can build tools
caption: One TikTok listed 20 free animation tools. My coding agents transcribed it, checked every link and license, judged each tool, and built the useful ones in Rust: a physics engine with a sound on every bounce, shape morphs, and a Manim math mode. Open source.

engagement.device: judgment invite: viewers pick the next tool
engagement.prompt: Which tool should we rebuild next?
engagement.pinned_comment: Name a tool or library you want rebuilt in Rust. I'll run it through the loop next.

scenes.narration: I watched one TikTok, and my coding agents turned it into this. Every bounce you hear is computed in Rust.
It starts when I save a Short that names some tools. This one promised twenty free tools for animation.
Then an agent parses it, like Claude Code, Codex, Grok or pi. It pulls the transcript and key frames, and checks every license.
Next comes the judgment, one tool at a time. Can an agent render it frame by frame, with no screen? Three of fifteen passed.

rows.text: Manim: animated math, used as is
Matter.js and Flubber, in our own Rust
12 others, each with a written reason

scenes.narration: Two of them we rewrote as our own Rust code. This shape morph is one of them.
The third one, Manim, we kept exactly as it is. Its math typography is too good to rebuild.
Every new tool ships with tests and measured results. The same scene renders to the same bytes every time.
That is the whole loop, and we run it every week or two. Watch. Parse. Judge. Build.
Everything is open source on GitHub. Which tool should my agents rebuild next?
